items.title: Harry Allen interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 13, 1997
items.q: hearing people like Scott or Buddy Tate or any number of guys

ctx.x: What was your college experience like for jazz? Do you think it made a big difference for you?

Well my reason for going to college, the main reason was to be around New York. I didn’t know anything about the Rutgers Jazz Program when I went there. I just wanted to be somewhere around New York City because I knew that the real way to learn how to play jazz was just to go and do it, and go and listen to guys and sit in and so that was my main focus on my four years of college was going to New York and hearing people like Scott or Buddy Tate or any number of guys. But the school, the Rutgers program was…
Did they have instances where — I know some people have complained about turning jazz study into so much technical stuff that it kind of works against your inspiration.
